coverage_note: Line-level content/technical review of Parts I-III (ch01-ch10 read in full, in book/manuscript/), checked against specs/python_capability_v0_1.md, specs/task_schema_v0_1.json, specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md, design/BOOK_DESIGN.md and review/PUBLICATION_REVIEW_INSTRUCTIONS.md, plus direct inspection of src/model/gpt.py, src/train/trainer.py, scripts/train.py, src/evaluator/evaluator.py, src/eval/evaluator_runner.py, src/evaluator/comparator.py, src/sandbox/sandbox.py, src/tokenizer/tokenizer.py, tests/sandbox + tests/gateway, artifacts/manifests/*.json, artifacts/datasets/pilot_{train,val,test}.jsonl + human_test.jsonl, docs/experiments/{stage1_pilot,stage4_composition,memory-not-run}.md -> stage1_pilot/stage4_composition/memorization, docs/decisions/leakage-finding-001.md, Appendix A and Appendix C, and ch14/ch15 for cross-references made from ch04/ch07/ch10. VERIFIED PASSING: parameter arithmetic 884,224 = 53,632 (291x128 + 128x128) + 830,592 (791,040 blocks + 2,048 block LayerNorms + 256 ln_f + 37,248 untied head) matches src/model/gpt.py and stage1.json exactly; dataset 1,400/300/300 with exactly 21 unique prompt strings and 21/21 train-test prompt overlap (matches ch09/ch10 tables and Appendix C novelty audit); 0.897 = 269/300 = 0.896666 in stage1_results.json; 0.88M usage; ch07's 0.875 = 525/600 consistent with ch15 (540/600 denominators appear only in ch11/ch15/ch21, outside this pass, and are consistent where referenced); ch08 initial-loss log(291)=5.67 vs 5.84; ch09 grad clipping (clip_grad_norm_ 1.0) and log_every=200 match trainer.py; ch06 comparator claims (float 1e-9 absolute, bool-not-int, order-insensitive dicts) match comparator.py; ch03/ch06 four-stage hierarchy and pass@1 definition match the protocol text; Appendix C correctly cites stage1_results.json for 0.897 and flags stage1.json as the pre-fix 0.000 run; ch02 keeps the four levels distinct and never collapses them; no pure catalog section found in ch01-ch10 (ch04 whitelist bullets and ch08 spec table each carry rationale); no ASD-STE100 or plain-language-standard claim exists anywhere in the manuscript, design, specs or README, so there is no compliance overclaim to correct (clarity reviewed qualitatively, see F-17). NOT CHECKED: rendered PDF/EPUB and figure pixels (Pass C), Parts IV-VII chapters in full, LaTeX build output, docs/failures beyond grep. 20 findings: 1 P0, 4 P1, 11 P2, 4 P3; no files modified.

findings.acceptance_test: The three excerpt rows equal hidden_tests entries of the named task_id in artifacts/datasets/pilot_test.jsonl (or the table is explicitly labeled illustrative and no longer described as what the judge runs).
findings.evidence: Enumerated all 8 matching records in pilot_test.jsonl (add_0036/0040/0041/0044/0045/0047/0050/0052, each 8 tests) and scanned every artifacts/datasets/*.jsonl for the three arg/expected pairs.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch10_does_it_actually_work.md - section 'One task, end to end', hidden-test excerpt table
findings.observed: The chapter presents a 'real run against the pilot model' and shows 'The hidden tests ... that the judge then runs. This task's suite has eight cases; here is an excerpt of three': (87,-98)->-11, (0,-24)->-24, (-6,0)->-6 for the prompt 'Implement solve so that given a and b it returns their sum.' The suite size (8) is correct, but none of the eight pilot_test.jsonl records carrying that prompt contains any of these rows; the pair (87,-98)->-11 exists in no record in any artifacts/datasets/*.jsonl; (0,-24)->-24 belongs to add_0054, which has a different prompt. The real rows for that prompt are e.g. add_0036: (-86,-95)->-181 basic, (0,-28)->-28 zero, (-1,-33)->-34 negative.
findings.required_correction: Replace the three rows with the actual hidden_tests of the named record (and name the task_id, e.g. add_0036), or relabel the table explicitly as illustrative and remove the claim that these are the tests the judge runs on this task.
findings.why_it_matters: Anti-fabrication is the book's bedrock rule (design/BOOK_DESIGN.md 12). A table of numbers presented as the scored run's hidden tests but absent from the scored dataset is exactly the defect the book says it never commits, and it is in the chapter that carries the headline 0.897.

findings.acceptance_test: specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 2 and ch03/ch10 state the same decoding condition for the primary metric, and the spec's version/status reflects the change.
findings.evidence: specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 2; ch03 'The success criterion'; ch08 'What the model is asked to do'; ch10 'What we measured: pass@1'; src/model/gpt.py generate(temperature=0.8, torch.multinomial); docs/experiments/stage1_pilot.md result heading.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch03_give_the_model_one_job.md ('The success criterion') and ch10 ('What we measured: pass@1'); vs specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 2
findings.observed: The book defines the primary metric as problem-level hidden-test pass@1 'under the evaluation's default temperature-0.8 sampled decoding' (ch03, ch10; ch08 confirms temperature-0.8 multinomial generation). specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 2 defines the primary metric as 'problem-level hidden-test pass@1 under deterministic/greedy decoding'. The code matches the book (gpt.py generate default temperature=0.8, torch.multinomial), so the protocol is the stale artifact, and the book never states a deviation from the protocol it cites as controlling.
findings.required_correction: Reconcile the two definitions in one direction: either reword/bump evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 2 to the temperature-0.8 single-sample protocol actually used (recording the version change), or have ch03 and ch10 state explicitly that these runs deviate from protocol v0.1's greedy primary metric and why. The canonical metric must not be defined two different ways.
findings.why_it_matters: Decoding condition changes the meaning of every pass@1 in the book; a reviewer cross-checking the canonical 0.897 against the controlling spec finds a direct contradiction in the definition of the primary metric.

findings.acceptance_test: ch04's stated conformance count equals the number of cases collected by the cited test file/command, and that run is recorded in an artifact or doc.
findings.evidence: tests/sandbox/test_sandbox.py (3 valid-program tests, 10 parametrized rejects, 1 syntax-error, 1 non-single-function = 15); repo-wide grep for '31'/'conformance'/'31-case' matches only book/manuscript, book/latex/_md, book/_epub.md, book/_assembled.md, README.md and the test file's docstring.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch04_build_a_world_we_can_control.md - 'Testing the world' (31-case conformance suite)
findings.observed: ch04 claims 'We build a conformance suite of 31 cases ... that is what our 31-case conformance run checks before we trust a single number it produces.' No artifact, doc, script or test file in the repository records a 31-case run: tests/sandbox/test_sandbox.py, the file whose docstring is 'Conformance tests for the sandbox AST whitelist + restricted execution', contains 15 cases (3 accept + 10 parametrized rejects + syntax-error + non-single-function), and the entire tests/ tree is 48 cases. The claim also says the suite has 'programs that use each allowed construct and must pass', but only 3 accept-path programs exist.
findings.required_correction: State the conformance count that is actually traceable (15 cases in tests/sandbox/test_sandbox.py) and cite the command/artifact that runs it, or add the missing conformance cases and record the run; keep the existing 'sample, not exhaustive proof' caveat.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the book's first 'we verified the instrument before trusting any number' claim. A specific, checkable count with no supporting artifact is an unverifiable quantitative claim and weakens the test-the-tester narrative it introduces.

findings.acceptance_test: Either scripts/train.py writes intermediate checkpoints at a stated interval with an artifact/failure-ledger entry showing one was used, or ch09 describes only the single post-training, pre-evaluation save and drops the 'saved us more than once' claim.
findings.evidence: scripts/train.py ('save model + manifest BEFORE evaluation so a crash doesn't lose training', single torch.save after train() returns); src/train/trainer.py train() contains no save; ls artifacts/checkpoints shows one stage1.pt; docs/failures/failure_ledger.md has no checkpoint entry.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch09_the_first_brew.md - 'Why the details of the training process matter' / checkpoint passage
findings.observed: ch09 states 'We use periodic training checkpoints that record the state at regular intervals during the run, so that a crash at step 1200 loses at most the steps since the last save ... So we keep intermediate checkpoints, not just a final one ... it has saved us more than once.' The implementation does the opposite: scripts/train.py performs exactly one torch.save of artifacts/checkpoints/stage1.pt after training completes and before evaluation, src/train/trainer.py never saves during training, only one stage1.pt exists, and no failure-ledger or manifest entry records an intermediate checkpoint save.
findings.required_correction: Either implement periodic checkpointing and record a real instance, or rewrite the passage to describe what the code does (a single post-training, pre-evaluation save) and remove or explicitly mark as hypothetical the 'saved us more than once' anecdote.
findings.why_it_matters: The chapter presents a practice and a personal outcome ('it has saved us more than once') as things the project did; neither is implemented or evidenced, which is a fabricated-results-adjacent claim under the anti-fabrication policy.

findings.acceptance_test: The executable column in ch10 equals the fraction of candidates that ran without runtime error under a definition shared by evaluator.py, the protocol and ch06 - or the column and both definitions are relabeled consistently everywhere the table appears.
findings.evidence: src/evaluator/evaluator.py line result['execution_ok'] = result['tests_passed'] > 0 or len(hidden_tests) == 0; specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 1 stage 3 and 2 metric list; ch06 'The four-stage pipeline'; ch10 results table.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch06_build_the_judge.md (stage 3 'Execution pass') and ch10 results table 'executable' column; vs src/evaluator/evaluator.py and specs/evaluation_protocol_v0_1.md 1-2
findings.observed: ch06 defines stage 3 as 'does it compile and run without error under the restricted environment' and the protocol defines 'executable success rate - fraction that execute without runtime error'. The implementation sets execution_ok = (tests_passed > 0), so a program that executes cleanly but fails every hidden test is reported as NOT executable. The 'executable' values reported in ch10's table (MODEL 0.897, TEMPLATE 0.900, RETRIEVAL 1.000) therefore mean 'passed at least one hidden test', not 'ran without error'.
findings.required_correction: Fix the evaluator to record execution success independently of test outcomes (e.g. no exception raised while running the tests) and re-derive the executable column, or relabel the column and ch06's stage-3 definition to the implemented quantity and apply the relabel everywhere the table appears (ch10, docs/experiments/stage1_pilot.md, Appendix C).
findings.why_it_matters: A headline results column is reported under a definition the code does not implement, so readers cannot distinguish 'the program crashed' from 'the program was wrong' - the exact diagnostic distinction ch06 says the four-stage funnel exists to provide.

findings.acceptance_test: Either evaluator.py reports syntax_ok and capability_ok from distinguishable checks (and the book shows both rates), or ch06 states that stages 1-2 are one combined validation gate and that the reported syntax rate includes capability rejections.
findings.evidence: src/evaluator/evaluator.py lines 33-41 (single try/except around sandbox.validate_source setting both flags); evaluator_runner.evaluate_candidates increments only syntax/executable/pass@1 counters.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch06_build_the_judge.md - 'The four-stage pipeline' (stages 1 and 2); vs src/evaluator/evaluator.py
findings.observed: ch06 says stage 1 (parses) and stage 2 (whitelist) are separate filters, that a smuggled import 'is rejected here' at stage 2, and that separating the stages 'tells us why a program failed'. The implementation calls sandbox.validate_source once inside a single try block and sets syntax_ok and capability_ok together, so a capability violation is recorded as syntax_ok=False; no capability rate is ever computed or reported. The 'syntax' column in ch10 therefore mixes parse failures with whitelist rejections.
findings.required_correction: Split the validator's error classes so syntax_ok reflects ast.parse success and capability_ok reflects whitelist acceptance (and report both), or amend ch06 to state that stages 1-2 are a single combined gate in the implementation and that the reported syntax rate includes capability rejections.
findings.why_it_matters: The chapter's central claim about the judge is diagnostic power ('it tells us where things go wrong'); as implemented, two of the four diagnoses cannot be told apart, so the claim overstates the instrument.

findings.acceptance_test: ch02 names all four canonical levels (Memorization, Distributional generalization, Surface generalization, Structural generalization) while still requiring them to be reported separately.
findings.evidence: Regex scan of book/manuscript/*.md: 'distributional' occurs only in ch16 and ch22; 'structural generalization' only in ch16; ch02 headings are 'Question 1 - Memorization', 'Question 2 - Same task, new examples', 'Question 3 - Same problem, different surface', 'Question 4 - New combination'; fig_ladder source in scripts/make_concept_figures.py uses 'Q2 NEW INSTANCES' and 'Q4 NEW COMBINATION'.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch02_what_does_it_mean_to_learn.md - 'The four questions of generalization' (and its figure fig_ladder.png)
findings.observed: ch02 introduces the four questions and correctly keeps them distinct and non-collapsible, but never uses two of the four canonical level names from design/BOOK_DESIGN.md 4: 'Distributional generalization' and 'Structural generalization' appear nowhere in ch02 (Q2 is 'Same task, new examples', Q4 is 'New combination'). Across the whole manuscript 'distributional' occurs twice (ch16, ch22) and 'structural generalization' once (ch16), so the taxonomy named in the design is essentially never named in the chapter that defines it, and its figure labels Q2/Q4 with the same non-canonical wording.
findings.required_correction: In ch02, label each question with its canonical level name (Memorization / Distributional generalization / Surface generalization / Structural generalization) alongside the plain-language question, and update the figure labels to match; keep the 'never mash these four into one number' rule intact.
findings.why_it_matters: The four-level taxonomy is the book's central framework and must never be collapsed; a reader who meets only ch02 cannot map its questions onto the terms used in the design and the later chapters, so the framework's identity is not established where it is taught.

findings.acceptance_test: Every quantitative claim from a real run in ch01-ch10 carries an evidence label, or design 11 states the single place labels live and the manuscript follows that rule consistently.
findings.evidence: Regex scan of book/manuscript/ch01-ch10 for all six labels returns zero matches per file; ch22 contains four [MEASURED] labels; design/BOOK_DESIGN.md 11; README.md Status section.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch01-ch10 (all ten chapters)
findings.observed: ch01-ch10 contain zero evidence labels ([MEASURED] [DERIVED] [DESIGN] [HYPOTHESIS] [INTERPRETATION] [UNKNOWN]), although design/BOOK_DESIGN.md 11 requires every quantitative claim from a real run to be marked [MEASURED] and the review instructions treat the six-level taxonomy as the book's own. Quantitative claims in these chapters (0.897, 884,224, 0.0208, 5.84, the 0.800/1.000 baselines, 59/60, 31 cases, 21 prompt strings) are all unlabeled; only ch22 uses labels (4 occurrences), so the convention is applied inconsistently across the manuscript.
findings.required_correction: Either add the correct evidence label to each quantitative claim in ch01-ch10 at first use, or amend design 11 and the review instructions to state that labels live only in the Appendix C registry and docs/experiments, and make ch22 conform to that single convention.
findings.why_it_matters: The evidence taxonomy is how the book separates measured from derived, designed and interpreted; without labels in the chapters that make the claims, a reader cannot tell which category a number belongs to, and the one chapter that labels (ch22) looks like an anomaly.

findings.acceptance_test: ch04's whitelist summary matches ALLOWED_BUILTINS/ALLOWED_NODES and spec 3/6, or explicitly defers to spec 6 as authoritative.
findings.evidence: src/sandbox/sandbox.py ALLOWED_BUILTINS (11 entries) and ALLOWED_NODES (includes Attribute); specs/python_capability_v0_1.md 3 and 6; ch04 'The capability spec' bullet list and following paragraph.

findings.observed: ch04 lists the permitted built-ins as 'abs, min, max, sum, len, range, int, float, round' and then states 'Everything else is rejected'. specs/python_capability_v0_1.md 6 and src/sandbox/sandbox.py ALLOWED_BUILTINS permit 11 built-ins - the listed nine plus `list` and `sorted` - and spec 3/6 also permit list methods append/count/index/pop via Attribute, which ch04's 'lists, indexing, slicing' bullet omits. findings.acceptance_test: The ch09 loss table's values are recoverable from an archived log/manifest cited in the chapter, or the intermediate values are marked as unarchived and only 0.0208 is presented as the recorded measurement.
findings.evidence: grep -rn '5.84|0.029' artifacts/ docs/ notes/ returns no matches; artifacts/manifests/stage1.json fields (final_train_loss 0.0208 only); Appendix C Stage 1 registry row text 'final loss 5.84->0.0208'.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch08_the_smallest_brain.md ('the initial loss was 5.84') and ch09_the_first_brew.md (step-by-step loss log)
findings.observed: ch08 reports an initial loss of 5.84 and ch09 prints an eight-line training log (5.84, 0.029, 0.022, 0.023, 0.020, 0.021, 0.019, 0.019). No archived source exists in the repository: grep of artifacts/, docs/ and notes/ finds no '5.84' or '0.029'; the only machine-recorded training number is final_train_loss 0.0208 in artifacts/manifests/stage1.json. Appendix C's registry row repeats '5.84->0.0208', so the book is internally consistent, but the intermediate values are traceable only to other book prose.
findings.required_correction: Archive the stage1 training log (or add per-step losses to the manifest) and cite that artifact in ch09, or state that only the final loss is machine-recorded and mark the intermediate curve values accordingly.
findings.why_it_matters: ch09's whole argument is that recorded configuration and logs make the run reproducible; an eight-value loss table with no archived log is the kind of untraceable quantitative claim the evidence taxonomy exists to flag.

findings.acceptance_test: ch10's memorization-control sentence reports 60/60 (train-record probe) and 59/60 (held-out/task-ID probe), matching memorization.json and ch14.
findings.evidence: artifacts/manifests/memorization.json; ch14 'The result' (60/60 train-prompt reproduction, 59/60 task-ID probe); Appendix C registry row 'Memorization ... 59/60 held-out'.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch10_does_it_actually_work.md - 'The shortcut audit', item 2 (Control (Ch14))
findings.observed: ch10 writes 'a probe of 60 pilot records and a held-out probe. On 59/60 it produced a passing general program, and on the held-out probe it emitted the general program rather than a memorized literal.' artifacts/manifests/memorization.json records pass1_train = 60/60 (train_n 60) and pass1_test = 59/60 (test_n 60), and ch14 reports 60/60 train-prompt reproduction with 59/60 on the task-ID probe. ch10 attaches 59/60 to the first probe, drops the 60/60 result, and leaves the two probes indistinguishable.
findings.required_correction: Restate as '60/60 on the training-record probe and 59/60 on the held-out/task-ID probe' (matching the manifest and ch14), naming each probe explicitly.

findings.acceptance_test: Each failure example in ch10 names the run/checkpoint/dataset it came from, and no example implied to be from the scored pilot evaluation is absent from pilot_test.jsonl.
findings.evidence: artifacts/manifests/pilot_manifest.json operations list; scan of pilot_test.jsonl for 'abs_add' (0 records) and for the reworded prompt string (0 records); docs/experiments/stage4_composition.md (abs_add is a Stage-4 composite); ch15 (reworded condition is the Stage-3 run).
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch10_does_it_actually_work.md - 'One task, end to end' (abs_add and reworded-surface failure examples)
findings.observed: The section opens 'here is a real run against the pilot model' and then presents two failure examples as part of that narrative without naming a run or checkpoint: the composite `abs_add` prompt yielding 'def solve(a, ab', and a reworded prompt ('...denoted p and q.') yielding 'def  a solve(a, b'. The scored pilot evaluation runs on artifacts/datasets/pilot_test.jsonl, which contains only the 10 primitive operations (no abs_add record) and only the 21 pilot prompt strings (the reworded prompt is not among them), so neither example can be an output of the scored pilot evaluation.
findings.required_correction: Name the exact run, checkpoint and dataset for each example (e.g. the Stage-4 composition run and the Stage-3 surface run, or an explicitly labeled demo generation), or move them out of the 'real run against the pilot model' framing; do not leave them implied to be pilot-evaluation outputs.
findings.why_it_matters: Evidence traceability: examples shown as what the pilot model did must be attributable to a recorded run, otherwise the chapter's most vivid failure illustrations are unverifiable and may be attributed to the wrong checkpoint.

findings.acceptance_test: ch10's cause list contains only mechanisms the runner can produce, and the sentence about where stop rules live matches the code.
findings.evidence: src/model/gpt.py generate() (loop of range(max_new), no EOS/PAD check); src/eval/evaluator_runner.py generate_code (max_new=80, NUL truncation, .strip()); ch10 'One task, end to end' and 'What we measured: pass@1'.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch10_does_it_actually_work.md - truncated-candidate caveat and the pass@1 methodology paragraph
findings.observed: ch10 lists the possible termination causes of the truncated candidate as 'the max_new limit, an EOS/PAD tie-out, the NUL-byte extraction boundary, or an unlucky sampled end', and states that 'max_new / stop policy / extraction rules live in src/eval/evaluator_runner.py'. That file implements only max_new=80 and truncation at the first NUL byte; src/model/gpt.py generate() always draws exactly max_new tokens and never stops on EOS or PAD, so an EOS/PAD tie-out cannot be a stop reason, and no stop policy exists to point at.
findings.required_correction: Remove 'EOS/PAD tie-out' from the cause list (or explain the mechanism if one exists), and either delete 'stop policy' or state that no stop policy is implemented - generation runs a fixed number of max_new draws and extraction truncates at the first NUL byte.
findings.why_it_matters: The passage is a model of honest hedging; listing a cause the code cannot produce, and citing a 'stop policy' that does not exist, undercuts the very discipline it demonstrates and misdirects a reader inspecting the runner.

findings.acceptance_test: docs/experiments/stage1_pilot.md describes the splits in a way consistent with pilot_manifest.json, pilot_{train,val,test}.jsonl and ch09/ch10 (same 10 operations, 21 shared prompt strings).
findings.evidence: docs/experiments/stage1_pilot.md Setup bullet; artifacts/datasets/pilot_manifest.json; operation sets and unique-prompt counts computed from pilot_train/val/test.jsonl; Appendix C novelty audit ('All three splits share the same 21 unique prompt strings').
findings.location: docs/experiments/stage1_pilot.md - Setup, 'Data' bullet (supporting record for ch09/ch10)
findings.observed: The Stage-1 experiment record states '1400 train / 300 val / 300 test (operation-disjoint splits)'. The dataset is not operation-disjoint: pilot_train, pilot_val and pilot_test all contain the same 10 operations and share all 21 prompt strings (verified directly from the jsonl files and confirmed by Appendix C's novelty audit). ch09/ch10 state the correct fact (test reuses the same 21 prompt strings), so the book is right and its own cited experiment record contradicts it.
findings.required_correction: Correct the stage1_pilot.md bullet to describe the actual split (same 10 operations across splits; 21 shared prompt strings; new task IDs and hidden-test inputs only), so the record a reader consults to verify ch09/ch10 agrees with the manuscript.
findings.why_it_matters: ch09 and ch10 stake their honest-scoping claim on the pilot reusing training prompts; the experiment record a reviewer opens to check that claim asserts the opposite, which reads as a contradiction of the book's central caveat.

findings.acceptance_test: No sentence in ch01-ch10 uses 'is the model' to mean exemplar without an explicit qualifier.
findings.evidence: ch03 opening section; ch05 opening section; ch08 'Why the simplest possible model'.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch03_give_the_model_one_job.md (opening) and ch05_build_the_teacher.md (opening)
findings.observed: ch03 opens its framing with 'A well-designed exam question is the model.' and ch05 with 'A teacher preparing worksheets for a test is the model.' The idiom means 'is the exemplar', but in a book whose central noun is 'the model' (the neural network) the sentences read as nonsense - ch03's is unreadable without the surrounding context, and the same construction recurs.

findings.location: book/manuscript/ch08_the_smallest_brain.md ('vocabulary: ~291 tokens') and ch09_the_first_brew.md ('a compact ~291-token vocabulary')
findings.observed: Two chapters write '~291 tokens' while ch08's own specification table, ch09's parameter split arithmetic (291 x 128 = 37,248) and artifacts/manifests/stage1.json (tokenizer_vocab 291) all give the exact count 291. The tilde implies an approximation where the value is exact and canonical.
findings.required_correction: Drop the tilde and write '291 tokens' in both places, matching the spec table and the manifest.
findings.why_it_matters: The book's discipline is exact, honest numbers; hedging an exact count with '~' is a small inconsistency in the same paragraph that insists on reporting the parameter split precisely.

findings.evidence: artifacts/datasets/pilot_manifest.json counts; record counts read from pilot_train/val/test.jsonl; scripts/train.py (loads val_tasks, never evaluates on them); ch09 'The data'; ch10 setup table; Appendix C denominator notes.
findings.location: book/manuscript/ch09_the_first_brew.md ('The data') and ch10 setup table
findings.observed: ch09 describes '1400 generated tasks' plus 'a separate 300-record test set', and ch10's table lists only Training (1,400) and Pilot test (300). The dataset and pilot_manifest.json record a three-way split of 1,400 train / 300 val / 300 test (also stated in Appendix C), and scripts/train.py loads the validation tasks but never evaluates on them. The 300-record validation split is never mentioned in Parts I-III.
findings.required_correction: State the three-way split in ch09 (and reflect it in ch10's table), noting that the validation split was not used for model selection if that is the case.
findings.why_it_matters: Omitting a split that exists in the artifacts makes the book's data description incomplete against its own manifest, and leaves open whether any selection was done on validation data.

findings.location: book/manuscript/ch07_build_the_rivals.md - closing result paragraph
findings.observed: ch07 says that under a wording change 'the model collapsed to 0.000 while the template system ... stayed at 0.875'. ch15's table shows the template baseline at 0.800 in-distribution and 0.875 on the reworded condition, and ch15 explicitly makes the point that the template 'gets better, not worse (0.875, up from 0.800)'. 'Stayed at' misdescribes a rise and disagrees with the chapter that owns the result.
findings.required_correction: Rephrase to 'rose to 0.875 (from 0.800 in-distribution)' or 'scored 0.875', matching ch15's table and reading.
findings.why_it_matters: Cross-chapter consistency of a canonical result: ch7's forward summary of the surface experiment should not contradict the number and its interpretation in ch15.
